nodes.label: Individual-per-org billing by default
nodes.rationale: Since billing groups, createOrgForUser silently auto-joins a user's second org onto their first org's subscription — surprising users who expected individual billing. Sharing becomes opt-in; the half-price discount is preserved when orgs share, only the trigger stops being automatic.

nodes.label: Dropping the auto-join is cap-safe
nodes.source_location: Why dropping the auto-join is cap-safe
nodes.rationale: The code comment claims the auto-join is what makes the community cap bite, but assertMayOwnAnotherOrg caps the total orgs a USER owns independently of grouping, and assertWithinGroupCap remains as a second, narrower gate on the explicit attach path. Dropping the auto-join removes nothing that protects caps — the load-bearing fact of the whole design.

nodes.label: POST /api/orgs attachToGroupId
nodes.rationale: Reuses attachOrgToGroup wholesale — zero new Stripe, charge or cap code — because a freshly-created org (community group, no live sub) is exactly its precondition. An attach failure returns HTTP 200 with {ok:false, reason}: the org already exists standalone, which is the safe default, and the UI explains it stayed on its own bill.

nodes.label: Eligible-group picker with attach preview
nodes.rationale: Eligibility mirrors attachOrgToGroup's gates; ineligible owned groups render disabled with the reason. A community group is never eligible because it holds exactly one org and is therefore always at cap. The exact charge comes from the existing attach/preview endpoint so the submit button can say 'Create & add — £X.XX now'.
